FNB SAFETY DEPOSIT ROBBERIES

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Bank robbers made off with over R300 million's safety deposit box raising questions about bank security.

Unique Selling Point:
WE HAVE EXCLUSIVE FOOTAGE OF ONE OF THE ROBBERIES INSIDE THE BANK

Summary:
Thieves stole 362 safety deposit boxes on December 18 from FNB’s Randburg branch

250 of the Randburg safety deposit boxes were discovered at a mineshaft in Laanglaagte – close to FNB stadium in Soweto.

A second robbery took place on Christmas Eve at Al Baraka in Fordsburg - no money was stolen, just a couple of computers.

Then on a third robbery hit New Year’s Eve at the FNB’s Parktown branch‚ where it is believed 30 boxes were stolen along with R1.7 million.

The losses are believed to be around R300 million.

We ask where it went wrong and why bank security was breached on this massive scale.


Further information:
THE GREY AREA:
The agreements governing the safekeeping of deposit boxes absolve FNB of any legal responsibility for the loss of the contents‚ but it could be liable if gross negligence was proved.

THE LAW:
“The Consumer Protection Act (CPA) provides that liability may not be excluded for gross negligence‚ regardless of the terms of a contract‚” said Tjakie Naude‚ professor of private law at the University of Cape Town.

As far as ordinary negligence was concerned‚ the CPA provided for the right to fair contract terms more generally‚ she said.

If gross negligence on the part of FNB was proved‚ the onus would be on the consumer to persuade the courts of the contents of the box and the value of those contents‚ since neither of these facts were necessarily disclosed to the bank in terms of the agreement‚ Naude said.

WHAT I’VE FIGURED OUT:
• THE KEY IS THE ARMED RESPONSE & MONITORING COMPANIES – usually they are two separate companies – in both the Randburg and Parktown cases – there was one company doing the monitoring and the armed response – and it both cases it was the same company - CHUBB.
• CHUBB SECURITY was involved in a similar robbery at an IT Warehouse in Midrand in September 2016. They were also the armed response & monitoring company. And the same MO was used. Cloned Chubb vehicle – footage of this
• In all four cases – the person who gets the call from the armed response company gets harassed prior to the robbery – so much so that the person eventually switches their phone off or stops taking calls from unknown numbers.

SAFE CONSTRUCTION
• Different categories have different specs – the bank decides what level vault they want to install
• Apparently it was at a category 5 – that means top notch – seismic detectors / motion detectors – if that was the case it doesn’t mean FNB off the hook – why didn’t it work

FOOTAGE
- In the bank in PArktown
- Exterior Randburg
- Footage of September robbery

Press Release:


Safety Deposit Box Heist
How did robbers make off with bank safety deposit boxes and content allegedly worth a whopping R100-million? Carte Blanche investigates the stealthy operation that saw thieves achieve a heist that’s left clients asking just how safe precious valuables are, when stored in bank vaults.


Script:


STRUCTURE BANK HEISTS

VO: When it comes to hard cash and priceless valuables, a new breed of bank robbers are not afraid to get their hands dirty.

In December last year, two Johannesburg FNB banks were hit in just two weeks by a gang of robbers, armed with crowbars, jackhammers and high powered drills.

INSIDER: This is professionals, it’s not amateurs It’s like a movie hey! You can’t believe the way they operate //

VO: The first target - FNB Randburg. 18 December 2016.
LOSSES: 362 Safety Deposit Boxes with an estimated value of almost R200 million

The second hit - FNB Parktown. 31 December 2016.
LOSSES: The contents of 48 Safety Deposit Boxes and R1.7 million in cash.

KELLY: People have now lost years and years of memories, a nest eggs, it’s their in case of emergency

VO: Kelly Fraser represents 180 FNB clients, affected by the heists in Randburg and Parktown. She says her father lost 50 Kruger Rands, valued at close to a million rand.

KELLY: It’s not about the money. It’s a long history of loyal clients that have been screwed over in this.

VO: Almost a month after the first robbery, FNB CEO Jacques Celliers broke his silence in a radio interview.

UPSOUND CELLIERS: “It’s certainly been a very tough and painful time for us to deal with – clearly we know and deeply regret the impact it has had on so many of our loyal customers, so it’s been a rough one.”

VO: Jacques Celliers declined to speak to us and neither does he seem to have spoken to any of the affected clients.

KELLY: If Jacques actually met them and spoke to them – then he would have something to say about empathy.

VO: ANJANI HARJEVEN’S safety deposit box was one of the 48 raided at FNB PArktown – it contained her family’s collection of jewellery dating back 5 generations.

ANJANI: // – we trust our money, lets trust them with our other valuables – I thought it was safest thing I possibly could, because they’ve got the infrastructure, I would think, to keep the stuff secure. INT3 M1


LINK: it goes beyond the price of a new diamond necklace or a new ring, it’s about what the jewellery represents – generations of hard work and legacies – taken and lost forever.

ANJANI: We have a family crisis, I feel completely responsible. There’s family entrusted you, my name is on the box, it doesn’t belong to me. (crying)

VO: Anjani’s family, like the majority of FNB victims, did not insure the items in the safety deposit box.

KELLY: None of these people did – why – because they thought it was safe in the bank.

VO: But the contracts governing the safekeeping of deposit boxes absolve FNB of any legal responsibility for the loss of the contents says Kalyani Pillay from the South African Banking Risk Information Centre.

KALYANI: the bank doesn’t know what you put it – so the fact that you put in it in a bank SDB is just mere a different place storing it

VO: The responsibility of insuring safety deposit box contents falls on the consumer says attorney Andile Nikani.

DEVI: BUT WHAT IF NEGLIGENT?
ANDILE: The bank will be liable in law - The bank will simply say, we did all we could to safe guard the contents, the fact that the system failed it may not point to the bank directly

LINK: Here at the Parktown branch - it’s believed that the robbers came in through a back palisade fence, through a small window into the bank – but this time they weren’t as clever, they left behind the DVR which contained the CCTV footage – plotting their every move.

VO: Here you can see the robbers entering the bank.

They turn off the lights as they make their way through the building

Once they get to the vault area, the robbers start drilling into the wall…

Then they stop for short while, it seems that they got some information.

Watch as this robber on the left, walks over to the safe door, and without much effort, he pulls it open! They’ve hit the jackpot

The gang casually raided 48 safety deposit boxes in the vault – forcing them open with crowbars.

They also managed to take 1.7 million rand in cash from the safe, making it a successful three-hour visit to the bank.

VO: BUT WHY WAS THE SAFE DOOR NOT LOCKED?

This footage is from the day before the heist.

You can see this FNB employee comes in numerous times to check the keypad on the safe door. She even returns with a colleague who uses a knife to fiddle with the keypad.

Then later, a third employee strolls in, pulls the door open, and closes it without locking the safe.

It would appear that the door’s locking mechanism was not working.

FNB have subsequently suspended three employees from the Parktown Branch.

KELLY: It’s supposed to be safe – they say it nine times in their brochure. Family heirlooms under lock and key – they lied to people.

VO: Andile points out that although negligence might be difficult to prove, the Consumer Protection Act may be the way to go for aggrieved clients.

ANDILE: CPA guarantees good quality service – //if the service falls under the standard or a reasonable expectation – they could sue under the CPA.

DEVI: You paid for a service, you didn’t get.
KELLY: Marketed as safe, paid for it because safe – now your fault for believing in the bank.

VO: The CPA also requires that a contract and its clauses are pointed out and explained to the client.

ANDILE CPA provides a way around contracts that are one sided, or that imposes obligations on customers or excludes liability on the side of the bank where the clients attention was not brought to it. INT3 M4

VO: A number of case studies say that’s not what happened when they signed up.

NALINI: And when we took the box – like a deposit slip – nothing saying if you are putting valuables there’s this clause and that clause.. INT3 M12

VO: The bank says that’s because “customers entered into agreements with FNB prior to the CPA taking effect.”

The bank also stated “After the CPA was enacted, FNB complied with the provisions of the CPA."

We decided to put FNB to the test and went to apply for a safety deposit box this week.

Despite spending almost an hour at the bank, neither liability nor insurance were mentioned to us – not even when signing the contract.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: “I’ve made a copy of the terms and conditions – please sign here”

VO: Nalini Naicker’s family safety deposit box was taken from FNB Randburg. It contained R1.5 million rands’ worth of Jewellery including items belonging Nalini’s late brother and sister.

NALINI: That box contained everything that was valuable to us!

VO: An evaluation was done in 2015 , but they couldn’t afford the monthly insurance premiums of nearly R3000

NALINI: I didn’t know what to tell my mother – you put it in my care, I put in the bank and now it’s gone.

VO: At FNB Randburg, it’s believed that the robbers spent around 12 hours breaking in and looting the bank vault without any interruptions.

LINK: We’ve been told that the robbers came in through the basement, drilled a hole through the toilet inside the bank and then just walked in.

VO: An insider, close to the investigation, is convinced there were people feeding the robbers internal information.

INSIDER: They must have a plan of that bank - because how did they exactly know where to start drilling with that jackhammer.

VO: In both bank robberies, the emergency contact persons were called incessantly prior to the break ins – they were harassed, sworn at and insulted – leading them to switch off their phones and missing the call from the alarm company.

While security vehicles are believed to have responded – no problems were reported. Our insider believes this no coincidence.

INSIDER: In this cases the monitoring company did the monitoring as well as the response
DEVI: So who is the monitoring company?
INSIDER: Chubb
DEVI: In all cases?
INSIDER: In all cases, the security are involved – there is no doubt about that.


VO: CHUBB declined an interview – saying they are bound by client confidentially and can’t comment on the incidents.

INSIDER: You get multiple signals which was supposed to go through on both banks – at least somebody, think about it - there’s big shit there!

LINK: It’s believed that the robbers cleverly disabled all the relevant cameras and took the onsite recording device, getting rid of all the CCTV footage of their time in the bank – they then made off with 362 safety deposit boxes [randburg]

VO: Days later 250 of those were discovered in Langlaagte, south of Johannesburg . Only some documents were discovered, but there was no sign of the valuables or the robbers.

NALINI: how can bank allow for this to happen? What kind of a security system does the bank have?

LINK: Sources tell us that apart from the security measures inside the bank, the exterior cameras weren’t working and the one guard that was on duty that night – was not employed by the bank, but by the landlord.

VO: The guard hasn’t been seen at work and seems to have disappeared.

While there are no regulated security standards for banks, Kalyani Pillay insists that the banking industry takes security very seriously.

KALYANI: They would look at various different layers of security – securing the building , there’ll be alarms, locks, physical security guards, cameras, so we have different levels INT1 M2

VO: Despite our repeated requests FNB declined an interview, saying “there are pending investigations.”

It appears that the bank finally took responsibility and issued a statement on Thursday saying:

“FNB will, despite not being legally obliged to do so, be initiating settlement discussions with uninsured customers.”
BUT it doesn’t come without limitations…
“…settlement discussions will depend on individual customers providing evidence regarding the contents of their safety deposit boxes…..”

ANDILE: The burden to prove the extent of the loss will fall on the customer – I’ve bought x, here is the receipt, it was in the box, I now need to be compensated.

ANJANI: you don’t have a receipt for a Kruger rand that someone received for payment - the world didn’t work like that back then.

VO: And the bank would know that if they had taken the time to speak to customers.

ANJANI: I feel violated // I feel really disappointed and I feel really hurt because I feel like a trust has been broken. // you can talk to me about insurance, clinically and intellectually we should have insured it, but what is the price on a pendant that was left to you by a great grandmother? (teary) and I trusted the bank with that.




PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Two FNB banks knocked in two weeks - robbers made off with close to 400 Safety Deposit Boxes containing millions of rands worth of irreplaceable items.

NALINI: That box contained everything that was valuable to us!

PROMO 2
VO: After robbers raided two FNB bank vaults in December - stealing safety deposit boxes with valuables worth millions of rands – affected customers are outraged and out of pocket.

KELLY: Marketed as safe, paid for it because safe – now your fault for believing in the bank.

PROMO 3
VO:

INSIDER: This is professionals, it’s not amateurs It’s like a movie hey! You can’t believe the way they operate //

KALYANI: They would look at various different layers of security – securing the building , there’ll be alarms, locks, physical security guards, cameras, so we have different levels INT1 M2 VO: Despite our repeated requests FNB declined an interview, saying “there are pending investigations.” It appears that the bank finally took responsibility and issued a statement on Thursday saying: “FNB will, despite not being legally obliged to do so, be initiating settlement discussions with uninsured customers.” BUT it doesn’t come without limitations… “…settlement discussions will depend on individual customers providing evidence regarding the contents of their safety deposit boxes…..” ANDILE: The burden to prove the extent of the loss will fall on the customer – I’ve bought x, here is the receipt, it was in the box, I now need to be compensated. ANJANI: you don’t have a receipt for a Kruger rand that someone received for payment - the world didn’t work like that back then. VO: And the bank would know that if they had taken the time to speak to customers. ANJANI: I feel violated // I feel really disappointed and I feel really hurt because I feel like a trust has been broken. // you can talk to me about insurance, clinically and intellectually we should have insured it, but what is the price on a pendant that was left to you by a great grandmother? (teary) and I trusted the bank with that. PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: Two FNB banks knocked in two weeks - robbers made off with close to 400 Safety Deposit Boxes containing millions of rands worth of irreplaceable items. NALINI: That box contained everything that was valuable to us! PROMO 2 VO: After robbers raided two FNB bank vaults in December - stealing safety deposit boxes with valuables worth millions of rands – affected customers are outraged and out of pocket. KELLY: Marketed as safe, paid for it because safe – now your fault for believing in the bank. PROMO 3 VO: INSIDER: This is professionals, it’s not amateurs It’s like a movie hey! You can’t believe the way they operate //

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Bank robbers made off with over R300 million's safety deposit box raising questions about bank security.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: WE HAVE EXCLUSIVE FOOTAGE OF ONE OF THE ROBBERIES INSIDE THE BANK
metadata.Summary: Thieves stole 362 safety deposit boxes on December 18 from FNB’s Randburg branch 250 of the Randburg safety deposit boxes were discovered at a mineshaft in Laanglaagte – close to FNB stadium in Soweto. A second robbery took place on Christmas Eve at Al Baraka in Fordsburg - no money was stolen, just a couple of computers. Then on a third robbery hit New Year’s Eve at the FNB’s Parktown branch‚ where it is believed 30 boxes were stolen along with R1.7 million. The losses are believed to be around R300 million. We ask where it went wrong and why bank security was breached on this massive scale.
metadata.Further information: THE GREY AREA: The agreements governing the safekeeping of deposit boxes absolve FNB of any legal responsibility for the loss of the contents‚ but it could be liable if gross negligence was proved. THE LAW: “The Consumer Protection Act (CPA) provides that liability may not be excluded for gross negligence‚ regardless of the terms of a contract‚” said Tjakie Naude‚ professor of private law at the University of Cape Town. As far as ordinary negligence was concerned‚ the CPA provided for the right to fair contract terms more generally‚ she said. If gross negligence on the part of FNB was proved‚ the onus would be on the consumer to persuade the courts of the contents of the box and the value of those contents‚ since neither of these facts were necessarily disclosed to the bank in terms of the agreement‚ Naude said. WHAT I’VE FIGURED OUT: • THE KEY IS THE ARMED RESPONSE & MONITORING COMPANIES – usually they are two separate companies – in both the Randburg and Parktown cases – there was one company doing the monitoring and the armed response – and it both cases it was the same company - CHUBB. • CHUBB SECURITY was involved in a similar robbery at an IT Warehouse in Midrand in September 2016. They were also the armed response & monitoring company. And the same MO was used. Cloned Chubb vehicle – footage of this • In all four cases – the person who gets the call from the armed response company gets harassed prior to the robbery – so much so that the person eventually switches their phone off or stops taking calls from unknown numbers. SAFE CONSTRUCTION • Different categories have different specs – the bank decides what level vault they want to install • Apparently it was at a category 5 – that means top notch – seismic detectors / motion detectors – if that was the case it doesn’t mean FNB off the hook – why didn’t it work FOOTAGE - In the bank in PArktown - Exterior Randburg - Footage of September robbery
